bodyMarkdown:
## What is the median salary in Australia?

When you ask **what is the median salary in Australia**, you are looking for the middle point of all salaries – not the average. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes both median and average earnings, but the on-site reference here uses average weekly earnings. For full-time adult ordinary time, the average is **$2083.70 per week** (May 2026). The median is lower because high incomes skew the mean. State differences also matter: earnings in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory tend to be above the national average, while Tasmania and South Australia are often below. The ABS provides state breakdowns, but the exact median varies by industry and location.

### How to convert hourly to annual pay

To estimate your annual salary from an hourly rate, use the formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a standard full-time role, we assume **38 hours per week** (the ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act). For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual figure is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,245.44**. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Fortnightly pay and tax

Your fortnightly gross pay is simply weekly pay × 2. For the minimum wage example, weekly pay is $1004.90 (38 hours × $26.44), so fortnightly is $2009.80. Tax is withheld by your employer using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not confirmed here). This is an estimate only; your actual tax depends on your circumstances.

### Minimum wage, awards, and casual loading

The **National Minimum Wage** is set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. Many workers are covered by **award rates** which are higher. Casual employees receive a **25% casual loading** on top of the base rate – that is $33.05 per hour for the minimum wage. When using [the timesheet](/) calculator, you enter your base hourly rate and check the box for casual loading; **do not** enter a rate that already includes loading. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (super guarantee), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

### State differences in ordinary-time earnings

The ABS Average Weekly Earnings survey shows that full-time adult ordinary time earnings vary by state. For example, the national average of $2083.70 per week masks higher figures in mining-heavy states or lower figures in retail-dominated regions. The **median salary** also differs: in New South Wales, the median full-time weekly earnings might be around $1,800, while in Tasmania it could be closer to $1,500 (these are illustrative; check ABS data for exact numbers). When you ask **what is the median salary in Australia**, remember it is not a single number – it depends on your state, industry, and occupation. The on-site reference provides national averages, not job-specific medians. For a tailored estimate, see [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

### Super and packaging

Super guarantee is **12% of ordinary earnings**, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It applies to most employees, including casuals, but stops once your earnings exceed $270,830 per year. Salary packaging can reduce your taxable income, but it is not included in this estimate. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Take-home pay considerations

Your take-home pay is your gross pay minus tax and Medicare levy. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help estimate net amounts. Remember that this calculator assumes no HELP debt, no Medicare levy surcharge, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination.

### Summary

When you look up **what is the median salary in Australia**, understand that the median is different from the average. The ABS average for full-time adults is $2083.70 per week, but the median is lower. State differences are significant. Use the hourly-to-annual formula with a 38-hour week to convert your rate, and remember that super is paid on top, casual loading is separate, and tax is progressive. For more precise calculations, refer to [the timesheet](/) or [average pay](/topics/average-pay).
